name: three.js r186 WebGPU (WebGPURenderer + TSL) headless in the cloud container, compared with WebGL2
environment_steps:
Working directory: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Aokigahara/f3a7dee1-ddd5-5966-b7a1-ff45901003d9/scratchpad/proto/web (P below). Setup: `ln -sfn ../../three186/package P/three` (three 0.186.0; `npm view three version` confirms 0.186.0 is the latest release). `ln -sfn /home/user/Aokigahara/viewer/assets P/ra` is a read-only link to the repo assets. `ln -sfn /opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright P/node_modules/playwright` lets the copied audit script resolve "playwright". Serve the scene with `python3 -m http.server 8799 --bind 127.0.0.1` from P (WebGPU needs http://, not file:// or about:blank).

Launch that works: chromium.launch({headless:true, executablePath:'/opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1194/chrome-linux/headless_shell' (the full build /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome also works), args:['--enable-unsafe-webgpu','--no-sandbox','--disable-dev-shm-usage','--enable-features=Vulkan','--use-vulkan=swiftshader','--use-angle=swiftshader','--ignore-gpu-blocklist','--disable-vulkan-surface']}). Load the createView 'swizzle' shim before three. Capture with canvas.toDataURL() straight after the last render, in the same task.

Scripts: probe P/probe.mjs (`node probe.mjs <set> [shell]`); scene P/forest.html plus runner P/run.mjs (`node run.mjs '<query>' <outName>`, for example `node run.mjs 'post=off&cam=0&sunel=48&hemi=2.2&exp=1.5&svmin=.08&hsky=%2380aaff&fogc=%234a6a92&fogk=0.4' t4_off_tuned`). Query keys: post=off|ao|ssgi, backend=webgpu|webgl, rays=0|1, frames, cam, sunel, sunaz, exp, hemi, skyk, svmin, infill, ts, gii, gir, fogc, fogk, fogd.

WebGL2 audit: `(cd /home/user/Aokigahara && python3 launch_viewer.py --port 8765 --quiet &)`, then `node P/audit_render.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8765/viewer/ P/audit P/cams_2.json 1280 800` (cameras C1_start_corridor and C3_offpath_trunks). Stop servers with `pkill -f 'http[.]server 8799'`. The bracket pattern stops pkill matching, and killing, its own shell, which a plain pattern did twice (exit 144). Both servers are now stopped.

Probe matrix (Chromium 141.0.7390.37, both builds gave the same result):
- A `--enable-unsafe-webgpu --use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader` and B `--enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan --use-vulkan=swiftshader`: navigator.gpu is present and the adapter is google/swiftshader (isFallbackAdapter, maxTextureDimension2D 8192, 19 features). A compute shader returns the correct output. Configuring the canvas fails with "A valid external Instance reference no longer exists", so these sets cannot present to a canvas.
- C (the recipe): adapter, compute and canvas present all work, and the canvas readback is correct (255,0,0,255).
- D `--use-vulkan=native --use-angle=vulkan` under xvfb-run, plus E/F variants with --disable-vulkan-surface and --use-webgpu-adapter=default: mesa-vulkan-drivers 25.2.8 was already installed. WebGL2 moves to ANGLE on Mesa llvmpipe (Vulkan 1.4.318). WebGPU still picks the SwiftShader adapter, and the canvas reads back blank (0,0,0,0). Lavapipe gives no WebGPU gain.
what_worked: Headless WebGPU works in this container only on the SwiftShader Vulkan adapter, and only with the recipe flag set (C). Sets A and B get an adapter and run compute but cannot present to a canvas. Native Vulkan (lavapipe) under xvfb helps WebGL2 only: WebGPU stays on SwiftShader and the canvas reads back blank. This applies to both the full chromium and chromium_headless_shell 1194 (Chromium 141).

A real-data scene renders with three r186 WebGPURenderer and TSL at 1280x800. Terrain is the repo GSI DEM (local-height.f32): a 2 m bilinear inner patch of 560 m plus the 8 m outer grid. The ground uses the moss and litter PBR from materials_v2 with a blend-noise mix and a normal map. The tree library (tree-library-v2.glb, 37 meshes, bark and alpha-tested foliage parts) is instanced from forest-instances.f32 within 520 m, using high, low and far LODs at 45 m and 230 m. On top of that sit about 4,200 infill trees to close the canopy, 326 saplings, 573 rock_* lava blocks and logs. In total that is 8.08 M instanced triangles in 74 instanced meshes, plus the SkyMesh sky, a 4096 PCF sun shadow over ±90 m, a hemisphere sky light, blue exponential haze and AgX tone mapping.

Lighting trick that works: a baked canopy sky-visibility map. Crown discs from the tree placements, with radii taken from the GLB bounding boxes, are splatted into a 512² map over ±520 m. Two box blurs of about 6 m follow, then sky visibility = exp(-3·coverage). The result goes in as material.aoNode, so it scales only the indirect sky light. Ground elevation is packed in the G channel, which lets tree materials lerp to full sky visibility with height above ground. This is a direct stand-in for a LiDAR canopy-height-model (DSM minus DEM) bake. Mean sky visibility is 0.31 and 0.027 at the C1 camera. With it the plain render (t4_off_tuned, t1_off) gets the UE5.8 frames' character: dark sky-occluded interior, dappled sunflecks from alpha-tested foliage shadows, bright sky gaps, cool blue distance, warm lit floor (highlight_blue_ratio 0.43).
Timings, WebGPU on SwiftShader at 1280x800, plain pass: first frame (pipeline compile) 19.7–33 s, steady about 19.5–20.3 s per frame; wall time per screenshot 34–90 s.

Timings for SSGI + TRAA + MRT (optionally with godrays): compile about 43–44 s, steady 26.8–28.3 s per frame. Godrays add almost nothing (27.6 s per frame without them). The earlier probe's placeholder cones ran at 0.65 s per frame plain and 1.8 s with SSGI at 960x600, so real content is about 15–30 times slower.

WebGL2 comparison, same TSL scene with forceWebGL: compile 29.9 s, steady 9.1–9.6 s per frame, so about twice as fast as WebGPU on SwiftShader. The ground is almost entirely black (see blockers), so it is not yet a like-for-like render.

WebGL2 comparison, the repository's own viewer via the copied audit_render.mjs: ready in 9.5 s. C1_start_corridor took 121.2 s wall (first camera, includes shader compile) and C3_offpath_trunks 23.1 s. Each frame is about 7.2–7.5 M triangles in 92–95 draw calls, 155 s in total. Output is in P/audit with audit.json.

three.js version and features: 0.186.0 is the npm latest. RenderPipeline replaces PostProcessing. addons/tsl/display contains SSGINode, GTAONode, SSAONode, TRAANode, TAAUNode, TemporalReprojectNode, DenoiseNode, RecurrentDenoiseNode, GodraysNode (shadow-map raymarched), SSRNode, SSSNode (screen-space shadows), BloomNode, DepthOfFieldNode, FXAA, SMAA, FSR1, SSAAPassNode, BilateralBlurNode, depthAwareBlend, Lut3DNode, OITPassNode and ImportanceSampledEnvironment. csm/CSMShadowNode is present for cascaded shadows. The core build contains VolumeNodeMaterial. There is no built-in auto-exposure or eye-adaptation node. PCFSoftShadowMap is removed in WebGPURenderer and falls back to PCFShadowMap with a warning.
lighting_stats.py scores. UE targets from frames g–j: log_avg_luminance 0.003–0.008, stops_p01_p99 8.5–10, sunfleck_fraction 0.07–0.16, shadow_blue_ratio 1.16–1.73. None of my renders meets all four.
t4_off_tuned (plain, cam 0): log_avg 0.0032 (met), stops 12.82 (not met), sunfleck 0.354 (not met, too many flecks), shadow_blue 4.01 (not met, too blue). It meets 1 of 4 but is visually the closest.
t1_off: log_avg 0.0009, stops 12.79, sunfleck 0.391, shadow_blue 1.00 (crushed black). It meets 0 of 4.
t0_off (sparse canopy, sun elevation 34°): log_avg 0.0301, stops 12.81, sunfleck 0.106 (met), shadow_blue 1.68 (met). It meets 2 of 4 but looks like an open park, not the valued look.
t6_off_cam1 (cam C3): log_avg 0.0007, stops 10.66, sunfleck 0.123 (met), shadow_blue 1.00. It meets 1 of 4.
SSGI renders t2, t5 and t7 have log_avg 0.05–0.10, stops 5.9–7.5, sunfleck 0.0005–0.023 and shadow_blue 0.25–0.32. They meet 0 of 4.
t3_webgl_off (WebGL2 backend): log_avg 0.0004, stops 12.80, sunfleck 0.300, shadow_blue 1.00. It meets 0 of 4.
Repository WebGL2 viewer: C1 scores log_avg 0.0324, stops 10.91, sunfleck 0.035, shadow_blue 0.53 (0 of 4). C3 scores log_avg 0.0193, stops 10.02 (met), sunfleck 0.028, shadow_blue 0.55 (1 of 4).
For reference, the UE g–j frames score log_avg 0.0033–0.0078, stops 8.49–10.16, sunfleck 0.067–0.156 and shadow_blue 1.16–1.73.
blockers: The screen-space GI path is broken in my scene and the cause is not found. Every RenderPipeline run (pass() with MRT, then SSGI, then TRAA, with or without godrays; t2, t5, t7) comes out 25–30 times brighter and flat. Sun shadows and the canopy sky-visibility effect both vanish, which loses the dappling entirely. Lowering the GI intensity from 6 to 1 did not fix it, and neither did removing godrays. The next isolation step is post=ao (GTAO only, no SSGI) to see whether the MRT pass itself drops shadows and aoNode; I did not run it because of the time box. Until then, SSGI and GTAO give no evidence for the look in this container.

The WebGL2 backend (forceWebGL) renders the same scene with the ground almost entirely black: only rocks, roots and a few flecks are lit. It looks like terrain self-shadowing or a shadow-comparison difference between backends, not yet investigated.

Tone and exposure are unresolved. Shadows crush to pure black (shadow_blue_ratio 1.00 is the EPS floor), which makes the dynamic range 12.8 stops against a target of 8.5–10. Raising the fill light with hemi 2.2, sky-visibility floor 0.08 and a blue sky colour overshoots to a blue ratio of 4.0. There is no bounce light: without working SSGI, sunlit ground does not warm nearby trunks. There is no auto-exposure (it would have to be written, for example as a log-average luminance reduction).

Fidelity limits carried over from the repo assets: sparse crowns in the tree library, which needed about 4,200 infill trees to close the canopy; no ferns or understorey foliage; no trails; terrain only 8 m DEM-smooth with no lava microrelief; rocks are simple blocks. The instance class to variant mapping was my own guess (class 0/2 as tsuga, 1/3 as hinoki, 5% snags).

Speed: SwiftShader WebGPU runs at about 20 s per frame plain and about 27 s with SSGI at 1280x800, with 20–45 s of shader compile per page load. Workable for a few verification stills per run, not for tuning loops of many frames or for animation.

Not done within the time box: volumetric fog or light shafts through VolumeNodeMaterial, CSMShadowNode cascades, TRAA convergence checks, a same-camera render of the UE baseline views. Only the 2 cameras C1 and C3 were rendered.
implications:
Agents can check WebGPU work themselves in this container. With the recipe flags, the SwiftShader adapter, an http:// page and a toDataURL capture, a three r186 WebGPURenderer and TSL scene built from real repo data (DEM terrain, PBR moss, the instanced GLB tree library, 8 M triangles, a 4096 shadow map) renders reliably in about 35–90 s per 1280x800 still. The same probe also gives agents a numeric check through lighting_stats.py. A render farm of this kind can verify composition, shadows and rough tone, but it is too slow for interactive tuning. Each iteration costs roughly 1–3 minutes per camera, so an agent workflow should batch a few fixed cameras per change and keep post-processing optional.

The WebGL2 path, both three's WebGL backend and the existing r180 viewer, runs about twice as fast per frame (9–10 s) but did not reproduce the scene faithfully: the ground went black. Lavapipe (native Vulkan) under xvfb speeds up only WebGL, not WebGPU.

On lighting parity, the owner's acceptance test, the evidence is mixed. A cheap baked canopy sky-visibility map (splatted crowns, blurred, fed into aoNode) plus alpha-tested foliage shadow maps already gives the UE5.8 character in a plain forward pass: dark occluded interior, sunflecks, bright sky gaps, blue distance. It hits the exposure-key target, but range and shadow colour are off, and none of the three renderers tested meets all four metric targets. This bake would transfer directly to the Yamanashi 0.5 m DSM/DEM (a canopy height model) on the Mac.

three's screen-space GI (SSGINode) exists, but in this build it destroyed the shadowing, cause not yet isolated. Real-time GI parity with Lumen is therefore not demonstrated. The honest claim is baked sky visibility plus shadow maps plus haze: about 60% of the valued look, and a better lit starting point than the existing r180 viewer, which scores 0 or 1 of 4 against 1 of 4 here and has blue ratios near 0.5.

Next steps: isolate the RenderPipeline or SSGI shadow loss (try post=ao, and SSGI without MRT diffuseColor). Add auto-exposure and a floor for shadow fill so the range drops to about 10 stops. Try CSMShadowNode and VolumeNodeMaterial for shafts. Always verify on the Mac's real GPU, where frame times should be real-time.

Nothing in /home/user/Aokigahara was modified by me. `git status` shows an untracked wicked_features.txt that I did not create.
